veranderings.rede: 'Rondom' is more natural than 'langs' for people near a smoker who breathe in the smoke; 'langs' suggests only someone right beside them.
An English word quoted as what someone calls a thing should be in quotation marks, which also shows it is not the lesson's own word.

veranderings.voor: Party mense sukkel om op te hou en
veranderings.na: Party mense sukkel om op te hou drink en
veranderings.rede: 'Om op te hou' has no object here; 'op te hou drink' says clearly what they struggle to stop, without adding content.

veranderings.blok: Medisyne wat jy sonder 'n dokter se brief koop
veranderings.rede: 'Medisyne drink' is colloquial and does not fit pills; 'gebruik' is the standard verb and covers all medicine.

veranderings.blok: Wat middels aan die verstand doen
veranderings.voor: die brein vra dan harder daarvoor
veranderings.na: die brein vra dan sterker daarna
veranderings.rede: 'Vra harder daarvoor' sounds like a translation of 'asks harder for it'; Afrikaans says 'vra na' and 'sterker' for a stronger craving.

veranderings.blok: Wat jy doen as iemand jou iets aanbied
veranderings.voor: want die skool en die kliniek help
veranderings.na: want die skool en die kliniek kan help
veranderings.rede: Bare 'help' at the end of the sentence sounds unfinished; 'kan help' is the natural way to say they are there to help.

beskerm_bedenkings.rede: The sentence before has 'Party kinders' as its subject, so 'Hulle' can at first read as the children rather than the damptoestelle; meaning is clear from 'bevat', so this is only a note, and 'Damptoestelle bevat meestal ook nikotien' would remove it if a person agrees.
